topic.title: Importing a Project with Existing Translations
topic.shortdesc: How to bootstrap the translation index for a project that already has translated content produced outside the AI translation workflow.

body.p: If a project already has translated content (produced manually, by a translation vendor, or by another tool), you do not need to retranslate it when you adopt the translation agent. Instead, have the agent record the existing translations in a translation index, so they are recognized as current rather than missing the next time you translate. See Running an Incremental Translation for what these statuses mean.

section.title: Building the Index for Existing Translations

ol.li: Start a translation job. In the Instructions field, tell the agent that the content is already translated and should be imported rather than translated, for example: The files are already translated. Import them into the translation index instead of translating them.

The agent pairs each translated file with its source file, following your project's layout (or explicit guidance you give it when the pairing is not obvious), and records an index entry for each pair using the source file's current Git blob SHA-1. No content is translated in this step; only the index is written.
Review the resulting index and translated files, then commit them.

section.title: Verify Before You Rely on It
section.p: Importing marks a translation as current without the agent checking its quality, so confirm the imported state before you depend on it:

ul.li: Spot-check that the imported translations match the source content at the revision recorded in the index.
Look for source files that have no matching translation; these remain missing and are translated on the next job.
If you are unsure whether a translation is still accurate, leave it out of the import (or delete its index entry) so the agent retranslates it instead of treating it as current.

body.p: This is a one-time preparation step. Once the index reflects your existing translations, later jobs follow the same incremental workflow as any other project.
